mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 2.5% (FEDFUNDS <= 2.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 2.5% (t-test of mean return against zero p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.0% (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates for equity valuation, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% (t-test of mean return against zero p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 105) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) signals an economic contraction that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 105 and UNRATE > 5.0% (t-test of mean return against zero p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized), rising housing starts (HOUST > 1000) signal strong consumer demand that supports equity valuations, producing positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and HOUST > 1000 (t-test of mean return against zero p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A payroll employment level above 137000 (PAYEMS > 137000) indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS > 137000 (t-test of mean return against zero p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) indicates weakening manufacturing activity, reducing corporate earnings growth expectations and producing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 100 (t-test of mean return against zero p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% annualized) and decrease in consumer credit (RSAFS < 380000) indicates a tightening monetary environment that raises discount rates for equity valuation, producing negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and RSAFS < 380000 (t-test of mean return against zero p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth rate > 3.0% annualized), rising housing starts (HOUST > 1000) indicate strong consumer demand that sustains corporate earnings growth, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 growth rate > 3.0% and HOUST > 1000 (t-test of mean return against zero p > 0.05).
